The factual matrix of the present case is that the plaintiffs are the actual and absolute owners of a built up property built on land ad-measuring 225 sq. yards (out of the total entire area measuring 300 sq. yards.) out of Khasra No. 28/11 and 28/20/1, situated in Lal Dora abadi deh village Mangolpur Kalan, Delhi earmarked in the year 1908-1909, (bearing Lal Dora certificate No.
SDM/KOT/RA/LalDora/83/857 dated 05.04.1983 as shown and marked red in the site plan annexed with the plaint.

That the plaintiffs purchased the suit property from Sh. Jai Prakash S/o Sh.
Kalpnath R/o WZ- 429, Sri Nagar, Rani Bagh, Delhi-110034 and Sh. Sho Raj Singh S/o Sh. Daya Nand R/o VPO Mangolpur Kalan, Delhi in July 1996 vide registered sale deeds.
That the plaintiffs are in the exclusive possession of the suit property as absolute owners since July 1996 i.e. from the date of purchase.
That the plaintiffs are engaged in business and there is a factory in the abovesaid suit property.

That on 16.12.1998 at around 12 P.M. in the afternoon, the demolition squad of the defendant no. 1 came and started demolishing the suit property i.e. Khasra No. 28/11 and 28/20/1 without giving prior notice.

That the demolishing squad of defendant no. 1 left the place around 4 P.M. on 16.12.1998 and threatened the plaintiffs that they would be coming tomorrow to demolish the rest of built up area of the suit property.

9. Issue wise findings as follows:-
Issue no. 1
The burden to prove this issue is on the plaintiffs.
In order to prove this issue, plaintiffs have relied upon the registered sale deed Ex. PW2/1.

Plaintiffs have examined Halqa Patwari of village Mangolpur Kalan as PW3 who had brought the Khatauni ownership of Khasra No. 28/20/1 which is Ex. PW3/1 in which the said khasra no. is shown as joint property of all villagers as per their share i.e. "REFAI AAM".

Ld. Counsel for judgement of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Gaon Sabha Budhela Vs. Dharam Singh, 25(1984) DLT 394. Section 8 of The Delhi Land Reforms Act,1954 and Rule 5 The Delhi Land Reform Rules,1954 give the absolute right to the villagers of the abadi deh land to transfer the same.

28/11 as shown in Ex. DW1/5 by 'pink' and in Mark A by 'parrot green' and same falls in 28/20/1.
It is admitted fact that land falling in Khasra no. 28/20/1 was not acquired.
Therefore, the defendant no. 1 DDA have not right over the said suit property and further have no right to demolish the same.
In view of these facts and reasons, issue no. 2 is decided against the defendants and in favour of the plaintiffs.
Issue no. 3.
The burden to prove this issue is on the defendant.

Section 53B of Delhi Development Act, 1957 provides for notice to be given of the suits and lays down that :-
(a) No suit shall be instituted against the Authority, or any member thereof, or any of its officers or other employees, or any person acting under the direction of the Authority or any member or any officer or other employee of the Authority in respect of any act done or made to have been done in pursuance of this Act or any rule or regulation made thereunder until the expiration of two months after notice in writing

has been, in the case of Authority, left at its office, and in any other case, delivered to,

7 or left at the office or place of abode of, the person to be sued and unless such notice states states explicitly the cause of action, the nature of relief sought, the amount of compensation claimed and the name and place of residence of the intending plaintiff and unless the plaint contains a statement that such notice has been so left or delivered.

(b) No suit such as is described in sub-section (1) shall, unless it is a suit for recovery o f i m m o v a b l e p r o p e r t y o r f o r a d e c l a r a t i o n o f t i t l e _______________________________________________________________________________________ CS SCJ 586/20148267/16 Sunil Kumar & Ors Vs. DDA & Ors Page no. 12 of 14 CNR No. DLWT03-000030-1998 thereto, be instituted after the expiry of six months from the date on which the cause of action arises.

sentences.text: (c) Nothing contained in sub-section (1) shall be deemed to apply to a suit in which the only relief claimed is an injunction of which the object would be defeated by the giving of the notice or the postponement of the institution of the suit.

Clause 3 of the said section specifically states that there is no need to give notice of the suit in which the only relief claimed is an injunction of which the object would be defeated by giving the notice or the postponement of the institution of the suit.
In the present case, the relief sought by the plaintiffs is of only injunction against the defendant DDA restraining them from further demolishing the suit property.

The very relief claimed by the plaintiffs shows that the object of filing the suit would be defeated by giving the notice as the defendant DDA can further demolish the property during the notice period without any restraining order from the Court.
No evidence has been led by the defendant pertaining to this issue.
Therefore, defendants failed to prove this issue.
Accordingly, the issue no. 3 is decided against the defendants and in favour of the plaintiffs.
Issue no. 4.

Since, issue no. 1 and 2 are decided in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants, the plaintiffs are entitled for relief of permanent injunction as prayed for restraining defendant no.1, its officials, employees, agents, servants, associates, assigns etc. from demolishing the suit property _______________________________________________________________________________________ CS SCJ 586/20148267/16 Sunil Kumar & Ors Vs.
